subject.title: Telegram owner commands: trusted execution mode for approval-gated actions

question: Should OpenClaw add a trusted-owner approval-bypass mode for Telegram group-origin privileged actions, and should it live as a shared execution policy rather than a Telegram-only boolean?
rationale: The request intentionally changes when privileged actions skip approval prompts in group chat, adds config surface, and crosses security/product boundaries that source inspection can identify but automation cannot choose safely.

options.title: Design Shared Trusted-Owner Policy
options.body: Add a disabled-by-default shared approval policy with explicit sender, allowlisted group, tool-class, destructive-operation, audit, docs, and regression-test semantics across the approval stack.

options.title: Keep Current Approval Model
options.body: Decline the bypass and document existing permissive exec/elevated modes as the supported low-friction trusted-operator workflow.

options.title: Add Telegram-Only Shortcut
options.body: Implement the proposed Telegram setting directly, accepting a smaller patch but higher risk of policy drift from shared approvals and elevated execution.

recommendation.title: Design Shared Trusted-Owner Policy
recommendation.body: Add a disabled-by-default shared approval policy with explicit sender, allowlisted group, tool-class, destructive-operation, audit, docs, and regression-test semantics across the approval stack.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision is primarily about product/security boundary policy and existing elevated/native approval behavior, both of which route through this recent history.
